excerpts:
The Stanley Cup is the oldest professional sports trophy in North America and is awarded annually to the champions of the National Hockey League. Named after Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada in 1892, the trophy has a unique feature. Unlike most awards, it is not recreated each year. Instead, the names of winning players, coaches, and staff are engraved directly onto the cup. As space fills up, older rings are replaced, allowing the tradition to continue while preserving its history. These examples show how the oldest trophy in sports continues to connect past traditions with present-day achievements, making them timeless symbols of excellence.

The Stanley Cup is the Oldest trophy in professional sports in North America. 

The original was just a silver bowl, donated by Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada, in the late 1800s. He bought it because his kids had fallen in love with the game of hockey and it was awarded to the best amateur hockey team in Canada. 🇨🇦 

Later, in the 1920s, the NHL adopted it as its most prized trophy. 

The original silver bowl lives in the hockey hall of fame.

results.title: The Stanley Cup Trophy - Topend Sports
excerpts:
The Stanley Cup is a championship trophy awarded yearly to the National Hockey League (NHL) playoff winners. The Stanley Cup The Stanley Cup The Stanley Cup is North America's oldest professional sports trophy. The trophy is named after Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada who donated it as an award to Canada's top-ranking amateur ice hockey club. There are three versions of the "Stanley Cup": the original 1892 bowl or Dominion Hockey Challenge Cup, the 1963 authenticated "Presentation Cup", and the 1993 "Permanent Cup" at the Hall of Fame. The Stanley Cup is engraved with the names of the winning players, coaches, management, and club staff.
